speech.howWeCountBody: A sentence counts when enough of its words were said and you added no extra words. The first try needs 90% of the words, the second 80%, and every try after that 70% — so a short sentence may need every word at first. Recognition slips are forgiven: missing Polish letters, one wrong letter in a longer word, the same sound spelled differently (“Bóg” → “bug”), and words written together or apart (“w niebie” → “wniebie”); a word heard as a different one only counts as not said, and filler sounds like “um” are ignored.

support.line: Teleo is free, with no ads and no tracking. If it helps you, you can buy its author a coffee.
support.buttonLabel: Buy the author a coffee — opens buycoffee.to in a new tab
support.note: buycoffee.to · opens in a new tab
support.tip1: Say each sentence at your own pace. I wait for you — never the other way round.
support.tip2: Five to fifteen minutes a day is the golden quarter-hour: enough to grow, short enough to keep.
support.tip3: Stuck on a name? Say it once more, slowly. After three tries you may skip it — that is all right.
support.tip4: Learning a new text? Turn on “Listen first” and hear each sentence before you say it.
support.tip5: Same time, same place: a habit grows best in the same soil.
support.tip6: Memory mode hides the words a little at a time — a gentle way to learn by heart.
support.tip7: A streak freeze covers a missed day. Rest does not undo the way you have walked.
support.tip8: Morning or evening — find the quiet part of your day and keep it for this.
support.tip9: Long sentences are split for you. Take a breath at each comma.
support.tip10: Words said aloud stay with you longer than words only read.
support.strip: Teleo is free · buy the author a coffee

dialogues.howToRead: it is spelt the English way, with the stressed syllable in CAPITALS (Polish stresses the last syllable but one). “zh” is the s in “measure”; “y” as in “yes”; “i” as in “bit”; “ee” as in “see”; “oo” as in “too”; “h” is breathier, like the ch in “loch”.

data.title: Your data
data.lead: Everything you do in Teleo is stored only in this browser on this device — no account, no server. A backup is a file you keep somewhere else and can restore on any device.
data.storageOn: The browser protects this data and will not delete it on its own. A backup still matters: a new phone, a cleared browser or a broken device.
data.storageOff: The browser may delete this data when space runs low — and Safari also after 7 days without opening the site. Install Teleo on your Home Screen and keep backups.
data.storageUnknown: This browser does not say whether it protects the data. Make backups regularly.
data.storageUsage: Teleo uses {{size}} (including the app, downloaded books and speech models).
data.storageGranted: The browser now protects Teleo's data
data.storageRefused: The browser declined for now — it usually agrees once Teleo is installed
data.backupHint: Keep a backup off this device: in Files or iCloud, on Google Drive or in an e-mail to yourself. Once a week is a good habit.
data.protectHint: A backup holds your prayers and your whole history. With a password nobody can read it — not in the cloud, not in your mail.
data.passwordWarning: Write the password down somewhere safe. Without it the backup cannot be restored — nobody, not even Teleo's author, can recover it for you.
data.share: Save to the cloud or send
data.whereToKeep: “Save to the cloud or send” opens the share menu: Files, iCloud, Google Drive, e-mail.

data.restoreHint: Replaces the data on this device with a backup file. You will see what the file holds before anything is replaced, and the data from before the restore stays here — you can undo it.
